methodological_rigor.justification: A well-designed preclinical study using the Hras12V transgenic HCC model with distinct intervention windows (4-month initiation cohort vs 6-month progression cohort), wild-type C57BL/6 safety cohort, blinded tumor counting, code-blinded histological assessment, randomization via random number generator, and IACUC approval. Strengths include the biosafety arm with hematology and liver/kidney chemistry panels, RNA-seq with appropriate DESeq2 thresholds and BH-adjusted q-values, and orthogonal validation (RT-qPCR, western blot, IHC for Ki-67). Limitations: only male mice used (authors acknowledge single-sex limitation), single-dose study without dose-response, sample sizes n=3-8 without formal power calculation (acknowledged), RNA-seq performed on peri-tumor tissue rather than tumors (authors justify but this complicates interpretation), and no in vitro mechanistic confirmation of p21 induction as direct VB2 effect.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: VB2 is widely available, inexpensive, and has a favorable safety profile; the concept of chemoprevention after HCC resection is clinically appealing, and HED calculation (about 12 mg/kg/day or 720 mg/day for adults) is within established high-dose clinical ranges for migraine prophylaxis. However, the data are entirely from a single transgenic mouse model with no human cell line, patient-derived organoid, or clinical data. LoE 5 (preclinical basic science). Translational path exists but requires extensive human validation.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript covers most ARRIVE items: animal housing conditions, ethical approval number (L20160315), randomization, blinding, group sizes, statistical methods, and adverse event monitoring. Explicit statement about minimizing animal suffering and 3R compliance is included. RNA-seq data handling (Q30, alignment rate, FPKM, BH correction) is well documented. Weaknesses: sex limitation is acknowledged but unaddressed in design, no pre-registration, supplementary tables referenced without clear repository accession, and no explicit data availability statement naming a public repository for raw RNA-seq data.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors position this as the first in vivo demonstration of high-dose VB2 monotherapy inhibiting hepatic tumorigenesis via retinol metabolism enhancement and G1/S cell cycle arrest. Prior VB2 oncology literature has focused on adjuvant or photosensitizer roles. The dual-phase retinol metabolism mechanism (Rdh16 upregulation + CYP2b/3a/4a induction yielding bioactive RA metabolites) is a novel conceptual framework supported by literature. The chemopreventive framing is distinct from existing VB2 research. Meaningful translational extension of prior VB2 oncology work.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with logical flow from phenotype to mechanism to safety. Figure legends are detailed and sample sizes are noted per panel. Discussion is balanced, explicitly acknowledging limitations (single sex, single dose, peri-tumor rather than tumor RNA-seq, indirect retinoid metabolite evidence). Minor issues include occasional awkward phrasing ('has an a robust inhibitory effect') and dense paragraph structure in the Discussion.

key_strengths: Well-designed two-phase intervention (tumor initiation at 4 months, progression at 6 months) in the Hras12V HCC model with parallel wild-type safety cohort
Blinded tumor counting with coded samples and randomization via random number generator
Orthogonal validation of transcriptomic findings via RT-qPCR, western blot (Cyclin D1/E1), and Ki-67 IHC
Comprehensive biosafety assessment (body weight, 12 hematology indices, ALT/AST/Crea/urea) with no observed toxicity at 170 mg/kg/day
First in vivo demonstration of VB2 monotherapy chemoprevention, with a novel dual-phase retinol metabolism mechanism linking Rdh16 upregulation and CYP-mediated bioactive RA metabolites
key_concerns: Only male mice studied; sex-dependent effects of VB2 acknowledged but not tested
Single VB2 dose (170 mg/kg/day) with no dose-response curve to define therapeutic window
RNA-seq performed on peri-tumor tissue rather than tumor; p21/Mcm findings may be partly attributable to reduced tumor burden
No in vitro HCC cell line confirmation of direct VB2-p21 causality (authors acknowledge)
No direct retinoid metabolite measurement to validate the proposed RA-derivative mechanism
RNA-seq raw data availability statement missing
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed preclinical transgenic-model study with blinded analyses and triangulated validation, offering a novel VB2 chemoprevention concept for HCC; limitations include single sex, single dose, and peri-tumor rather than tumor transcriptomic analysis, placing it comfortably in Tier 3 with minor revisions.
